title: Exact-release noncommensurate scheduler trajectory equivalence
hypotheses: The compiled RM11 production scheduler emits exactly the preregistered noncommensurate target and solve-boundary sequences.
Exact Ribasim records allocations at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20 hours when driven by the production scheduler route.
The scheduler route and independent explicit-reference route reproduce Basin level and cumulative root/external UserDemand transfer at every emitted accepted target within frozen tolerances.
The naive 6-hour control records only the initial t=0 allocation, reproducing the H10 call-start aliasing mechanism.

The scheduler route changes day-end total physical UserDemand delivery by more than 1 m3 relative to the naive control, showing the scheduling correction is hydrologically material in this frozen topology.
For each route, cumulative UserDemand delivery plus Basin storage change closes against the 32 m3 one-day source supply within 0.05 m3.
failure_rule: Do not alter the target sequences, allocation-record expectations, materiality threshold or route-equivalence tolerances after exact-release execution. Repair only technical setup failures.
nonclaims: No MODFLOW or RibaMod composition is required because H10 already established that the aliasing mechanism resides in the Ribasim BMI call-start semantics for this release.
No canonical admission by RM12 alone.
